meta.title: Lunar Landing Site Navigator - site catalog

coordinate_types.lander_position: Measured position of the landed spacecraft (orbital imaging / mission navigation).
coordinate_types.region_representative_point: Representative point inside a ~15 x 15 km candidate landing REGION. NASA publishes Artemis III candidates as regions, not points; replace with official region polygons when available.

categories.artemis_iii_candidate: NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole (Oct 2024 set of nine)
categories.commercial_clps: NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) robotic landers
categories.international: Robotic landings by non-US space agencies

visibility.method: DE440 + MOON_ME (app.astrodynamics); smooth 1737.4 km sphere, NO terrain masking
visibility.criterion: any part of the disk above the local horizontal (el > -semidiameter)

sites.name: Tranquility Base
sites.coordinate_source: NSSDCA Apollo landing site coordinates (Wagner et al., Icarus 283, 92-103, 2017; LROC)
sites.description: First crewed lunar landing (Armstrong, Aldrin). Equatorial mare plain, ~1.8 km basaltic regolith terrain; Earth permanently high in the sky (~66 deg elevation), continuous direct-to-Earth line of sight.

sites.name: Hadley-Apennine
sites.coordinate_source: NSSDCA Apollo landing site coordinates (Wagner et al., Icarus 283, 92-103, 2017; LROC)
sites.region: Palus Putredinis, at the foot of Montes Apenninus beside Hadley Rille
sites.description: First J-mission and first Lunar Roving Vehicle. Mare/highland boundary next to the Apennine front and Hadley Rille; returned the 'Genesis Rock' anorthosite.

sites.name: Taurus-Littrow
sites.coordinate_source: NSSDCA Apollo landing site coordinates (Wagner et al., Icarus 283, 92-103, 2017; LROC)
sites.region: Taurus-Littrow valley, south-eastern rim of Mare Serenitatis
sites.description: Last crewed landing to date (Cernan, Schmitt - first scientist on the Moon). Deep highland valley; discovered orange volcanic glass at Shorty crater.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.coordinate_source: Approximate massif location; NASA has published regions, not point coordinates
sites.description: ~5,000 m massif on the near-side limb with near-continuous sunlight on its summit and slopes descending ~8,000 m toward permanently shadowed terrain. Earth hovers near the horizon, so DTE visibility depends strongly on libration and local terrain.

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.coordinate_source: IAU/Wikipedia feature centre of Mons Mouton (84.6 S, 31.0 E)
sites.region: Lunar south pole, between Nobile and Manzinus
sites.description: Flat-topped mountain rising ~6,000 m; its broad plateau (separate 'Mons Mouton Plateau' region) is the widest, flattest Artemis candidate. IM-2 Athena landed on it in March 2025.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1
sites.coordinate_source: Estimated from Nobile crater geometry (centre 85.2 S, 53.5 E; D = 73 km), south-western rim
sites.description: Rim terrain rising ~3,000 m on Nobile's south-western side, adjacent to Nobile's permanently shadowed floor (VIPER's former target area).

sites.name: Nobile Rim 2
sites.coordinate_source: Optimal-site point from a multi-criteria Artemis III site study (ResearchGate 385942633)
sites.description: North-eastern rim of Nobile at about -1,400 m, the second-lowest Artemis candidate; close to large permanently shadowed regions of interest for volatiles.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 2
sites.coordinate_source: Estimated: de Gerlache crater longitude (87.1 W) at the published ~50 km distance from the pole
sites.description: Closest Artemis candidate to the pole (~50 km), on a rim rising ~3,000 m above its surroundings beside de Gerlache's permanently shadowed interior. At this latitude Earth grazes the horizon; DTE is intermittent and terrain-limited.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena
sites.coordinate_source: Landed position (84 deg 47'26" S, 29 deg 11'45" E); LROC intended site was 84.78 S, 29.13 E, landing ~250 m off target
sites.region: Mons Mouton plateau, lunar south pole
sites.description: Southernmost lunar landing to date. Athena came to rest on its side in a crater ~250 m from target; carried the PRIME-1 ice drill/mass spectrometer and the Grace hopper. Mission ended after ~1 day due to poor solar-panel illumination.

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 'Ghost Riders in the Sky'
sites.coordinate_source: LROC landing region centre (18.56 N, 61.81 E); Firefly reports touchdown within its 100 m target ellipse
sites.description: First fully successful commercial lunar landing (upright, all 10 NASA payloads operated). Ran ~14 Earth days through lunar day and imaged a lunar sunset and an eclipse of the Sun by Earth.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 / Statio Tianhe
sites.coordinate_source: Liu et al., Nature Communications 10, 4229 (2019); LROC independently gives 45.457 S, 177.589 E (+/- 20 m)
sites.region: Von Karman crater, South Pole-Aitken basin (FAR SIDE)
sites.highlight: FAR SIDE: Earth never rises here. Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication window = 0%. All lander/rover traffic is relayed through the Queqiao satellite at Earth-Moon L2.
sites.description: First soft landing on the lunar far side. Deployed the Yutu-2 rover, the longest-operating lunar rover. Because the Moon is tidally locked and libration is only ~+/-8 deg, Earth stays 37-52 deg below this site's horizon at all times (DE440, 18.6-yr cycle).

sites.name: Chang'e 6
sites.region: Apollo basin, South Pole-Aitken basin (FAR SIDE)
sites.highlight: FAR SIDE: 0% direct-to-Earth window; relayed via Queqiao-2.
sites.description: First sample return from the lunar far side (1,935 g).

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 / Shiv Shakti Point
sites.region: High southern latitudes, between Manzinus C and Simpelius N
sites.description: First landing at high southern latitude (Vikram lander + Pragyan rover); in-situ detection of sulfur by LIBS.

sites.name: SLIM
sites.coordinate_source: JAXA-reported landing position (~55 m east of the planned point)
sites.region: Slope of Shioli crater, near Mare Nectaris
sites.description: Pinpoint-landing demonstrator: touched down within ~100 m of target (main-engine anomaly left it upside-down). Survived several lunar nights.
